summary: Franklin County, AR tower known from a directory entry quoting a 1934 newspaper account of a wooden tower; marked removed, with no date or builder found.

facts.status_note: Directory marks it as removed; no removal date given

events.note: July 1934 visitors' account quoted by the directory: one-mile foot trail to a wooden tower, said to be about 340 feet tall; that height comes from this account only

evidence.supports: tower in Franklin County, Ozark National Forest
the visitors' account is dated July 1934
the account is attributed to the Fayetteville Daily Democrat
one-mile foot trail; wooden tower of about 340 feet; ranger assured the visitors it was safe to climb
evidence.quote: We took a foot trail that led one mile to the tower. The mile was soon covered and we arrived at the tower. It was about 340 feet and made of wood, but the Forest Ranger assured us that it was safe to climb.

evidence.supports: directory marks the tower as removed, with no date

notes_for_editor: Single source: a directory page quoting a 1934 Fayetteville Daily Democrat item. The 340 ft height is from that item alone, so it is in the event note only, not in facts; the record has no height. A Forest Service page for a Black Mountain fire lookout (recid 71975) came up in search but timed out twice (HTTP 504) and was not read, so its location is unconfirmed. Search results for Black Mountain also returned towers in other states, which were excluded. No corrections proposed. Story is short because the evidence is thin.
